Scenario

70% of people think cake is better than pie. 30% of people think pie is better than cake. 10 active voters in the thread What the comment section is like now (roughly)

+7 ↕ Cake is better than pie! +3 ↕ Pie is better than cake! How comments would be if ↓ was for disagreeing

Hey guys, I only have a handful of stories to tell, and I've told most over on that other website, but to help get this place off the ground, I'll be reposting them here. Let's get this party started.

I work for a small IT shop that will take most jobs, big and small. Most of our work is network and pc repair/building for businesses not big enough for their own IT, but we get a good number of personal machines as well. Y'know, just all-around freelance.

Our customer today, $Lawyer, sold his offices a few years ago when he discovered he can do everything from home. $Lawyer's wife is a court reporter who does the same.

Their printer got old and broke and a few weeks ago we got them a new one. Got a call today saying it wasn't working for some reason. They both had to leave the house at the moment, but could I look into it. His main computer has LogMeIn, so I remoted in to check it out. The software was saying that either it was out of paper or there was a jam. I called back to ask if they had seen the error and checked these things and was told they had loaded paper, but didn't know how to check for jams. Whatever, fair enough.

$L: "Are you free to just come out and look at it?"

$Me: "I guess. Is anyone there to let me in?"

$L: "Yeah $15yoSon is there."

They happen to live a few blocks away, so I head over and check it out. When I got there, there was not only a jam, but it caught my eye immediately. I'm not sure how you could not see it just by glancing. On many printer trays there's a little extender that flips out. Apparently it was flipped down and a page had caught underneath it, thus causing a backup and subsequent jam. To make it better, the drawer for adding paper is directly below the tray, so for them to have checked if there was paper, they would have had to essentially ignore the jam in front of them.

Photo for the curious.

I don't know, I try to understand users, but sometimes there's nothing to do but sigh. Whatever, I get paid and their printer was fixed. Now I'm off to save the rest of the world.
At least it didn't take too much out of your time!
